title: Cheese Risotto
lede: No rinsing the rice, no pot, just one frying pan. Instead of ladling in stock bit by bit the traditional way, this simplified version adds all the water at once and simply simmers.

tools.name: Frying pan (about 24 cm)
tools.note: Handles everything from frying to simmering.

tools.name: Wooden spatula or cooking chopsticks
tools.note: For stirring the bottom while it simmers.

tools.name: Measuring cup
tools.note: A 500 ml bottle filled to about 80% works too.

tools.name: Lid
tools.note: For an extra steam if the rice is still chalky at the end.

steps.title: Cut and fry the bacon
steps.text: Cut the bacon into 1 cm strips, put them in a dry frying pan, and cook over medium heat for about a minute. The fat that renders out becomes your cooking oil.

steps.title: Add the rice, unwashed
steps.text: Tip in the rice as-is and stir for a minute, until every grain is coated in fat. When the rice turns faintly translucent, that's enough.
steps.hint: Rinsing washes off the surface starch, and with it the creaminess. For risotto, unwashed is correct.

steps.title: Add the water and bouillon all at once
steps.text: Pour in 400 ml of water, drop in the bouillon cube, and break it up with the spatula as you stir. Turn the heat to high and bring it to a boil.

steps.title: Simmer on low for 15 minutes, stirring now and then
steps.text: Once boiling, drop to low heat and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes. Give it a slow stir from the bottom about every 3 minutes.
steps.hint: Skip the stirring and the bottom scorches. Keep the heat low and stay close to the stove.

steps.title: Taste and adjust the liquid
steps.text: Crush a grain of rice and check it. If the center is still chalky, add 50 ml of water and simmer 3 minutes more. If it's soupy, raise to medium heat for about a minute to drive off the excess.

steps.title: Off the heat, stir in the cheese and butter
steps.text: Kill the heat first, then add the 2 tablespoons of grated cheese and 10 g of butter and stir for about 20 seconds. Season with salt and black pepper, and it's done.
steps.hint: Add cheese over a live flame and it splits, leaving a grainy texture.

troubleshooting.solution: The heat was too high. Drop it to the lowest setting and stir every 2 minutes instead. Don't stir the burnt layer in. Scoop only from the top when serving.
Not enough water. Add 50 ml at a time and check every 3 minutes. A lid speeds things up, but traps moisture, so take it off and reduce for a final minute.
Raise to medium heat and reduce for about a minute while stirring. It tightens a little from residual heat after plating, so stop while it's just slightly loose.
A scant teaspoon of salt plus a teaspoon of mentsuyu (if you have it) stands in. The bacon brings salt too, so hold back and adjust by taste at the end.
Two sausages or a can of tuna works instead. For tuna, add it oil and all, and halve the butter.
